version.title: The graph of tangent
card: For any angle, \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\). When \(\cos x = 0\), this fraction is undefined, so \(\tan x\) has no value at that angle.

Cosine is 0 at \(90^{\circ}\), \(270^{\circ}\) and every \(180^{\circ}\) on from these. At each one, the graph of \(y = \tan x\) has a vertical asymptote: a line the curve gets closer and closer to but never meets.
Between two asymptotes, the curve rises from left to right, with no highest or lowest point. It crosses the x-axis where \(\sin x = 0\): at \(0^{\circ}\), \(180^{\circ}\), \(360^{\circ}\) and so on.
The same shape repeats every \(180^{\circ}\), so the period of \(y = \tan x\) is \(180^{\circ}\), half the period of sine and cosine. For example, \(\tan 225^{\circ} = \tan 45^{\circ} = 1\).

2.alt: The graph of \(y = \tan x\) for \(x\) from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(360^{\circ}\). Dashed vertical asymptotes are at \(x = 90^{\circ}\) and \(x = 270^{\circ}\). Between the asymptotes the curve rises from left to right. It crosses the x-axis at \(0^{\circ}\), \(180^{\circ}\) and \(360^{\circ}\).

version.remember: Asymptotes where \(\cos x = 0\), at \(90^{\circ}\) and every \(180^{\circ}\) on. The shape repeats every \(180^{\circ}\).

a.q: Why does the graph of \(y = \tan x\) have a vertical asymptote at \(x = 90^{\circ}\)?
a.why: Since \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) and \(\cos 90^{\circ} = 0\), the fraction has 0 on the bottom, so \(\tan 90^{\circ}\) is undefined. It is true that \(\sin 90^{\circ} = 1\), but that does not cause the asymptote: the zero on the bottom does.
a.clue: Look at the bottom of the fraction \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\).

b.q: How many vertical asymptotes does the graph of \(y = \tan x\) have from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(720^{\circ}\)?
b.why: Cosine is 0 at \(90^{\circ}\), \(270^{\circ}\), \(450^{\circ}\) and \(630^{\circ}\), one every \(180^{\circ}\), so there are 4. The answer 5 counts the x-intercepts at \(0^{\circ}\), \(180^{\circ}\), \(360^{\circ}\), \(540^{\circ}\) and \(720^{\circ}\) instead.
b.clue: List the angles up to \(720^{\circ}\) where \(\cos x = 0\).

rejected.title: The tangent graph
card: The graph of \(y = \tan x\) comes from \(\tan x = \sin x \div \cos x\). It repeats every \(180^{\circ}\), so its period is \(180^{\circ}\).
When \(\cos x = 0\), the fraction cannot be worked out. The graph has a vertical asymptote there, a line it gets closer to but never touches.

In one period from \(-90^{\circ}\) to \(90^{\circ}\), the asymptotes are at \(x = -90^{\circ}\) and \(x = 90^{\circ}\). Others are at \(x = 270^{\circ}\), \(x = -270^{\circ}\) and so on, every \(180^{\circ}\) apart.
The graph crosses the x-axis where \(\sin x = 0\), so at \(x = 0^{\circ}\), \(180^{\circ}\), \(-180^{\circ}\) and so on. Between each pair of asymptotes, the curve rises from left to right.

3.alt: The graph of \(y = \tan x\) with x in degrees. Between each pair of vertical asymptotes the curve rises from left to right. The dashed asymptotes \(x = -90^{\circ}\) and \(x = 90^{\circ}\) are marked on the x-axis. The curve crosses the x-axis at \(-180^{\circ}\), \(0^{\circ}\) and \(180^{\circ}\).

rejected.remember: \(\tan x = \sin x \div \cos x\): period \(180^{\circ}\), with asymptotes wherever \(\cos x = 0\).

a.q: Which of these angles gives a vertical asymptote on \(y = \tan x\)?
a.why: At \(x = 90^{\circ}\), \(\cos x = 0\), so \(\tan x\) cannot be worked out and there is an asymptote. At \(x = 180^{\circ}\), \(\sin x = 0\) and \(\cos x = -1\), so \(\tan 180^{\circ} = 0\) and the graph crosses the x-axis there.
a.clue: Look for the angle where \(\cos x = 0\).

b.q: There is a vertical asymptote at \(x = 90^{\circ}\) on the graph of \(y = \tan x\). Where is the next one to the right?
b.why: Asymptotes repeat every period, which is \(180^{\circ}\). So the next one is \(90^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 270^{\circ}\). The angle \(180^{\circ}\) is tempting, but \(\tan 180^{\circ} = 0\) there, so the graph crosses the axis.
